Definition: a beholder in vision; also a compact (as looked upon with approval)
BiblicalUsage: A seer is one who sees what God shows, and Gad is called David's seer when the word of the LORD comes to him. The prophets and seers warned Israel again and again to turn from evil, and the history of Solomon's reign is written in the records of the seers. Seeing is not guessing: it is receiving, and then speaking what was received.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God has always spoken through seers, not because He needs a mouthpiece, but because His people need to hear. The seer's job is plain — see truly, speak plainly, and leave the results to God. I hold that every believer is called to something like it: to see what God is doing and to say so.
